title: The Slight Edge
short_description: Jeff Olson on how simple daily disciplines compound — success and failure are usually slight edges repeated.
chapter_titles: Chapter 12: Start smaller than ego wants

questions.question_text: What is the slight edge idea?
questions.option_b: Small daily disciplines or neglects compound into success or failure

questions.question_text: Why is the beginning of the success curve hard?
questions.option_b: Results lag while reps feel pointless — people quit in the flat part

questions.question_text: What does ‘easy to do, easy not to do’ mean?
questions.option_b: The valuable little actions are optional-feeling, so people skip them

questions.question_text: What helps adherence?
questions.option_b: Philosophy, momentum, environment, reflection, and teaching others

questions.question_text: How should you size a new slight edge?
questions.option_b: Smaller than ego wants — unbeatable consistency first

title: The Richest Man in Babylon
short_description: Clason’s Babylonian parables of money — pay yourself first, make money work, and protect capital.
chapter_titles: Chapter 2: A part of all you earn is yours to keep
Chapter 5: Own where you live theme

questions.question_text: Pay yourself first means?
questions.option_b: Save a portion before lifestyle spending

questions.question_text: How should you invest per the spirit of the book?
questions.option_b: Put money to work carefully in understandable ways; protect capital

questions.question_text: Besides saving, what raises wealth?
questions.option_b: Increasing ability to earn via skill and reliability

questions.question_text: Guard against loss emphasizes?
questions.option_b: Protecting capital from foolish unexplained risks

questions.question_text: Best modernity check?
questions.option_b: Automated saving, debt control, emergency fund, skill growth, prudent investing
questions.option_d: Only gold coins under mattress without plan

title: Peak
short_description: Ericsson’s science of expertise — deliberate practice, mental representations, and why greatness is grown.

questions.question_text: What characterizes deliberate practice?
questions.option_b: Stretch goals, focus, feedback, and refined repetition

questions.question_text: What are mental representations?
questions.option_b: Expert pattern models that compress complexity

questions.question_text: What does Peak say about prodigies?
questions.option_b: Early advantage is largely accumulated structured practice — greatness is grown

questions.question_text: How handle plateaus?
questions.option_a: Only grind the same error harder blindly
questions.option_b: Redesign drills and challenges to update representations

questions.question_text: 10,000 hours slogan?
questions.option_a: Exact magic number for all domains always
questions.option_b: Oversimplifies — quality, coaching, and structure matter more than raw hours

title: Man's Search for Meaning
short_description: Viktor Frankl’s Holocaust memoir and logotherapy — finding meaning even in suffering, and freedom in choosing one’s attitude.
chapter_titles: Chapter 1: The camp and the question

questions.question_text: What freedom does Frankl emphasize even in extremes?
questions.option_a: Freedom to escape any camp at will
questions.option_b: Freedom to choose one’s attitude and response

questions.question_text: What is logotherapy primarily concerned with?
questions.option_b: Helping people find meaning

questions.question_text: When is suffering meaningfully engaged in Frankl’s sense?
questions.option_b: When unavoidable — seek dignity/meaning; when avoidable, change the cause

questions.question_text: What is the existential vacuum?
questions.option_b: Emptiness and boredom when meaning is lacking, often filled poorly by stimulation

questions.question_text: What does tragic optimism include?
questions.option_b: Facing pain, guilt, and death honestly while still saying yes to meaning

title: Breath
short_description: James Nestor on how we breathe — nose vs mouth, CO2, ancient techniques, and why breathing is a missing pillar of health.
chapter_titles: Chapter 1: The forgotten organ of focus
Chapter 6: Chewing, soft food, and airways

questions.question_text: What breathing default does Breath emphasize for most daily life?
questions.option_b: Nasal breathing when safe

questions.question_text: Why does CO2 matter in Nestor’s framing?
questions.option_b: Breath chemistry and comfort relate partly to carbon dioxide balance; overbreathing can worsen air hunger

questions.question_text: What should you do if you suspect sleep apnea?
questions.option_b: Seek medical evaluation — summaries are not diagnoses
questions.option_c: Only breathe through the mouth harder

questions.question_text: What is a practical daily approach?
questions.option_b: A simple morning–midday–night breath stack with tracking

questions.question_text: For easy athletic work, what does the summary suggest?
questions.option_b: Train nasal breathing in easy zones; mouth when intensity demands
